Do brain-inspired mechanisms help continual reinforcement learning?

Mostly no, with two specific exceptions.

We tested seven brain-inspired ideas one at a time, each against a matched control that is not brain-inspired, in small agents that learn a sequence of tasks. Every number on this page is read from the frozen results.

What we builtScorecardWatch the agents ForgettingMemory trade-off

What we built

An agent that sees a small grid world, turns each frame into spikes, optionally remembers the last few frames, and picks an action. It learns tasks one after another. The sleep variant alternates online learning with offline phases that revisit stored experience.

Swap one part at a timeEach ablation changes one component: spiking vs ordinary (CNN) encoder, with or without Transformer memory, local learning rules on or off.
Matched controlsSleep is compared with replay, which uses the same buffer interleaved with online learning, and with EWC, naive fine-tuning and one network per task (isolation).
Fair budgetsSame frames, seeds and learning rate across arms; replayed samples matched exactly for sleep vs replay; memory counted as parameters plus buffer.
